A $7 billion expansion was announced to grow the Council Bluffs campus and establish a new Cedar Rapids, Iowa data center. Google also cites a NextEra Energy agreement tied to restarting Iowa's Duane Arnold nuclear plant as part of its regional power strategy, and $1.3 million toward a 47-site water quality/grade stabilization project.

reading.body:
Google does not publish the megawatt capacity, square footage, or building addresses for its Council Bluffs facility in Pottawattamie County. The company discloses only aggregate investment figures at the state level, reporting over $20 billion invested in Iowa since 2007 and a $7 billion expansion underway to grow Council Bluffs and establish a new Cedar Rapids campus. This opacity means the actual compute density and AI hosting capability of this location cannot be derived from Google's public statements.

Among Iowa's 52 mapped data center facilities, only two operators publish individual site power figures, totaling 18 MW across the state. This campus ranks third by published megawatts in Iowa, but that ranking reflects an absence of published data rather than a measured capacity. The Council Bluffs site anchors Google's largest regional data center investment and is paired with a major nuclear power agreement involving the restart of the Duane Arnold plant, suggesting material scale relative to the rest of the state, but the scale itself remains undisclosed.

Whether this campus matters to AI scaling depends on Google's compute deployment choices, which are not public. The company's $20 billion Iowa commitment and coordinated power infrastructure strategy indicate strategic importance to its operations. Without published power consumption or machine count, external observers cannot assess how this facility constrains or accelerates Google's AI training or serving capacity relative to other Google campuses or competitors.
